title: SLO-driven chaos curriculum and capacity simulation guidelines
author: Marco Reynolds
content:
Overview

This document defines a repeatable curriculum and operational guidelines for SLO-driven chaos/gameday exercises and capacity simulations. The goal is to exercise realistic multi-tenant inference failure modes, validate SLOs and error-budget controls, and collect forensic evidence suitable for incident review and actionable remediation. This guide is intentionally lightweight so teams can run 1–2 hour labs or full-day rehearsals with equivalent outcomes.

Goals

- Validate that production SLOs reflect customer-impacting outcomes.
- Confirm autoscale and capacity policies behave under realistic traffic and model-serving degradations.
- Exercise fallback and graceful degradation (model variants, region failover, cache priming).
- Collect structured evidence and metrics for post-event analysis tied to deployments, rollouts, and model changes.
- Train on controlled abort and rollback criteria to avoid customer harm.

Scope and audience

- Audience: SREs, runtime engineers, platform owners, and on-call partners.
- Systems: Redwood inference serving runtime, request router, cache layer, autoscaler, and per-tenant priority controls.
- Not covered: billing/accounting reconciliation (separate finance runbook).

Prerequisites

1. Testbed environment with traffic replay capability (see Tooling).
2. Canary dataset and representative token-length distribution for workload.
3. Owner sign-off and scheduled maintenance window (if exercises touch production).

Key definitions (for this curriculum)

- Target SLOs: 99.9%% p95 latency for short-text generation routes; 99%% p99 for embedding batch jobs; availability SLOs per-tenant remain as defined in SLO registry.
- Error budget window: 30 days rolling; exercise will consume a controlled percentage (target 5–15%%) for tabletop calibration.
- Capacity simulation run: a synthetic traffic injection with stepwise load, introduced faults, and validation windows.

Curriculum overview (modular)

1. Quick warm-up (30–45 minutes)
   - Objective: Ensure team familiarity with telemetry dashboards and evidence collection.
   - Activities: Walk the SLO dashboards, confirm alert subscriptions, run a 10-minute synthetic baseline replay.

2. Mini chaos lab (1 hour)
   - Objective: Simulate a single-fault cascade and validate graceful degradation.
   - Faults injected (choose one): KV cache eviction, model quantization path misconfiguration, or network routing flapping between regions.
   - Expected outcomes: Fallback to smaller model variant, increased token cost but preserved critical responses, clear SLO delta.

3. Capacity simulation (1.5–2 hours)
   - Objective: Measure autoscaler headroom and service tail-latency under increasing concurrency and long-context traffic.
   - Steps: Stepped traffic ramp: 25%%, 50%%, 75%%, 100%% of projected peak; hold intervals 10 minutes. Introduce a 10-minute throttling event at 75%% to validate token-priority arbitration.

4. Complex multi-tenant scenario (2–4 hours)
   - Objective: Validate tenant isolation, fair-share heuristics, and emergency eviction procedure.
   - Scenario: One tenant spikes with emergent batch embedding jobs while other tenants run steady low-latency requests; test backpressure and eviction policies.

5. Post-exercise tabletop & evidence handoff (45–60 minutes)
   - Objective: Capture lessons, map root causes, and generate remediation tickets with owners and SLO impact.

Tooling and artifacts

- Traffic replay: load-generator with token-length and event-time fidelity (recommended: replayer v2). Example CLI: replayer run --trace sample.json --scale 1.4 --duration 20m
- Failure injection: failctl (network, process, latency, and memory faults). Example: failctl inject --target runtime-node-3 --type socket-delay --ms 250
- Telemetry dashboards: SLO overview, p50/p95/p99 latency heatmap, per-tenant error budget burn, request-router traces, KV hit/miss.
- Evidence collection: standardized evidence bundle (see Evidence Matrix). Script: evidence-collector --scope exercise --output /tmp/evidence-<YYYYMMDD>.tgz

SLOs and error budget policy for exercises

- Pre-declare the error budget allocation for the exercise: annotate the SLO registry with an exercise token and approval.
- Target consumption: small labs 1–5%%, full-day rehearsals 10–15%%.
- Hard abort: if cumulative error budget > 25%% for any production tenant without explicit exec approval, abort exercise and roll back injected faults.

Capacity simulation configuration table (recommended baseline)

| Parameter | Recommended value | Rationale |
|---|---:|---|
| Baseline multiplier | 1.0 | Normal traffic profile |
| Peak multiplier | 1.5–2.0 | Simulate high demand bursts |
| Ramp step | 25%% increments | Small enough to observe inflection points |
| Hold duration | 10 minutes | Capture steady-state metrics for each step |
| Long context ratio | 10–20%% | Models with KV-cache pressure show different tails |

Runbook: executing a standard simulation (checklist)

1. Pre-checks (15–30 minutes)
   - Confirm owners, communication channel (pager, slack), and maintenance windows.
   - Snapshot current SLO status and evidence baseline.
   - Ensure replay traces and canary keys loaded.

2. Start baseline replay and validate dashboards (10 minutes)

3. Execute traffic ramp (operators: run replayer with step schedule)

4. Inject single-point faults at planned time markers; observe autoscaler and fallback behavior

5. Collect evidence bundle at each stage and tag with step id and timestamp

6. If abort criteria triggered: run abort procedure (see Abort & Rollback)

7. Post-run verification: validate services restored, caches re-primed, and model-variants pinned back if changed.

Abort & Rollback (safety gates)

- Abort triggers (any of the following):
  - Tenant-level error budget > 25%%
  - Uncontrolled memory pressure causing OOM restarts across > 10%% of serving nodes
  - Data-plane errors that corrupt persisted KV cache state
- Immediate steps on abort:
  1. Halt traffic generator and failctl scripts.
  2. Revert injected network/process faults.
  3. Verify core runtime health, then escalate to on-call SRE lead if not recovered within 10 minutes.

Evidence Matrix (minimal fields)

Each evidence bundle must include the following items and be named consistently:
- exercise-id: string (e.g., slo-chaos-20260112-01)
- dashboard-snapshots: list of png/csv exports with timestamps
- trace-exports: tracing spans correlated to exercise windows
- node-metrics: cpu/mem/gpu-utilization CSV
- autoscaler-events: raw events log
- injected-faults-log: failctl output
- sample-requests: 50 raw request/response pairs from each affected tenant (sanitized)

Attachment naming convention: <exercise-id>_<artifact-type>_<YYYYMMDDTHHMMZ>

Post-exercise retro template (minimum required fields)

- Summary (one paragraph): what we set out to test and the outcome.
- SLO impact: quantifiable delta and error-budget consumption.
- Root cause hypothesis: top 1–3 contributors.
- Evidence pointers: artifact filenames and timestamps.
- Action items: owner, priority, due date.

Ownership and run cadence

- Exercise owner: service steward listed in SLO registry (primary contact).
- Recommended cadence: team-level mini-labs quarterly; full cross-functional rehearsals semi-annually.

Measurement and success criteria

- Success: clear mapping from injected faults to SLO telemetry where mitigation patterns performed as designed (fallback invoked, degradation prioritization enforced).
- Secondary success: reproducible remediation steps and closed action items for the top remediation tickets within 30 days.

References and related pages

- See: Chaos exercises library: /confluence/eng-sre/reliability-initiatives/chaos-exercises-and-failure-hypothesis-library-2026
- See: Capacity rehearsal runbook: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/capacity-rehearsal-decision-playbook-2026

Appendix: quick checklist for on-call (cheat sheet)

- Before exercise: publish exercise id, start time, and abort thresholds to #sre-gameday.
- During: stream evidence bundle to shared storage every 15 minutes.
- After: file retro within 48 hours and annotate SLO registry with consumed budget.

Contact

For questions or to schedule a cross-team rehearsal, contact Marco Reynolds (marco@redwood.example) or the eng-sre scheduling channel.
